built_from: elsewhere: justETF section tabs that jump the page (the founder, 2026-11-06)
reason: A person keeps a sense of where things are; when the page moves without their doing, they lose their place and have to find it again.
negative_check: planted clean controls in browser mode (sp500 pc, study fund phone)
held-out benchmark noise, with and without
status: in v1, the default reviewer since 2026-11-06 (browser sessions only)

result.runs: runs/candidate-moving/without and runs/candidate-moving/with (identical but for behaviour); personas first-job-phone and careful-retiree-pc, repeat 2, reader effort medium, graders high

p15_caught_in_first_10.note: every p15 session in both arms received the plant as a moved: line (sp500: 42 px up after the years; keren: the year control moving 69 px), so the gap is the instruction, not delivery; one-sided Fisher p about 0.004

justetf_tabs.note: not a test of the instruction: one session per arm got HTTP 429 and saw no page; in the with arm none of the three loaded sessions clicked a section name, in the without arm two did, were told the page scrolled 3,389 and 1,230 px, and did not report it. Other justETF keys 0 of 4 in both; j-help (liked) complained of in 2 of 4 in both

false_alarms.rule: a finding about movement the session was never told of in a moved: line, or about something not on the screen

movement_findings.with: 10 in 8 sessions, every one matching a moved: line that session received
detail: S&P 500 pc, 4 of 4 sessions: part of the screen jumped sideways on the first change of an input (115 px; the real defect of issue #200)
study fund phone, 4 of 4 sessions: the fields reshuffle when switching to self-employed (288 px up; real on the live page)
study fund phone, 1: a link at the top scrolled the page 2,784 px by itself (an in-page jump, real)
study fund phone, 1: the page scrolled 140 px when the year slider was moved; possibly the tool: act.mjs focuses an ARIA slider with el.focus() and no preventScroll, which can scroll the page itself

cost_usd.justetf_flag_graders: not recorded by grade-flag.mjs; about 0.5 estimated (32 grader calls)

result.verdict: Keep as a candidate that generalises: with the instruction p15 is caught 6 of 8 against 0 of 8 without, and the clean controls gain no false alarms (their new movement findings are all real and grounded, among them issue #200, missed 0 of 4 without). The justETF tabs were not exercised in the with arm, so that part is unanswered. It enters a version only after the held-out benchmark shows no rise in noise and no fall in catch rate. Cost to watch: movement findings take a place among the first 10 (44 findings in both arms, so another finding gave way).

held_out.runs: runs/baseline-1/reviewer (without) and runs/baseline-1/moving (with, run-moving.json: run-reviewer.json plus the behaviour file); 39 held-out screens, still screenshots only, personas first-job-phone and careful-retiree-pc, one run each, reader effort medium; graded with grade-flag.mjs on the same 52 case files (keys rebuilt from the reviewer arm's grading stamps), two blind graders at high effort, a third on a split

gained: hg-tax-after-six (careful-retiree-pc, rank 7, settled by a third grader)

held_out.grader_agreement_with: 102 of 104 pairs (kappa 0.93); 2 splits, both hg-tax-after-six, settled by a third grader

moved_jumped_shifted.note: five findings in the with arm use 'jump', 'move' or 'pushed' figuratively (eye jumps, numbers jump out, a box moves on to another topic, an explanation pushed aside in the layout); none says the screen moved

detail: s03 first-job-phone, rank 1: 'The sticky bar with tabs appeared on top of the text while I was scrolling and covered what I was reading' (no scrolling was seen; the bar is drawn mid-picture because the slice is taller than a phone screen)

s27 careful-retiree-pc, rank 4: 'A popup appeared over the list and covered what I was reading' (the popup is open in the picture by design; the reviewer arm described the same box as covering, with no event)
s28 first-job-phone, rank 6: 'a nav bar ... suddenly covers the middle of the list'
appeared_in_time.note: the instruction itself counts something appearing as the page moving; the first is a clear claim of an event on a still screen, the other two are event wording over something the picture does show

held_out.verdict: Not passed. The catch rate holds: 14 of 72 against 13 of 72 on the headline single run (allowed fall: 2), pooled 10 against 8 of 36, McNemar p = 1.00 (3 lost, 4 gained). But the instruction did not stay silent on still screens: one finding claims a bar appeared while the reader was scrolling (s03, rank 1), and two more use appearance wording ('appeared', 'suddenly') for overlays the pictures show. No finding claims a move, jump or shift. Noise needs the founder's sample and is not judged here.

decision.what: attached only in browser mode (panel.mjs "behaviourBrowser"); still screens never get it
decision.why: movement can be perceived only by a session that uses the page; on still screens the instruction has nothing true to report and produced the one false claim (s03, a header the capture drew mid-page, called a bar that appeared while scrolling). In browser mode it caught the planted jump 6 of 8 against 0 of 8, was silent where nothing moved, and its 10 findings on clean pages were all real moves (among them #199 and #200). The held-out catch rate held (14 against 13 of 72), so the instruction costs nothing measurable there.

noise.result: none of its three findings was called 'would not bother anyone': n07 (a tab that scrolls the page by itself) a real problem; n02 (fields that change places when a choice changes the form) and n03 (a sideways jump while typing) can't tell
noise.his_note_n02: the aggressive redrawing is abrupt for the eye, but the whole page does need to change; a subtle redraw or animation would make it less abrupt; not that big deal
